description.text: Leidos Holdings, Inc. (“Leidos”), a Delaware corporation, is a holding company whose direct 100%-owned subsidiary and principal operating company is Leidos, Inc. Leidos was founded in 1969 by physicist Dr. Robert Beyster. Since our founding 57 years ago, we have applied our expertise in science, research and engineering in rapidly-evolving technologies and markets to solve complex problems of global concern. We use the terms “we,” “us” and “our” to refer collectively to Leidos Holdings, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. Leidos is an industry and technology leader serving government and commercial customers with smarter, more efficient digital and mission innovations. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, with 47,000, global employees, we pursue strategic growth across five pillars: space and maritime; energy infrastructure; digital modernization and cyber; mission software; and managed health services. Our customers include the U.S. Department of War (“DoW”), the U.S. Intelligence Community, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (“DHS”), the Federal Aviation Administration (“FAA”), the Department of Veterans Affairs (“VA”) and many other U.S. civilian, state and local government agencies, foreign government agencies and commercial businesses.

analysis_md:
# LDOS — Leidos Holdings, Inc.
v5.4 run, 2026-10-16. In scope (market cap $16.2305B at $124.85, nasdaq_quote_api — under the $40B cutoff).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
US government technology and services contractor: IT modernization, cyber, intelligence mission support, defense systems (incl. Dynetics hypersonics/air defense), health and civil programs. Revenue is overwhelmingly US-government contracts — fixed-price, cost-reimbursable and time-and-materials — won and re-won through competitive procurement. Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-07-03): revenue $4.56B, up 7.2% YoY (organic +3.9%, the rest largely the Entrust acquisition), adjusted EPS $3.26, adjusted EBITDA margin 13.8%, bookings ~$4.9B (book-to-bill 1.1; Defense segment 2.2), backlog $48.71B (+5.4% YoY) with funded backlog $10.22B (+44% YoY). Management raised FY2027 guidance at the print: revenue midpoint $18.3B, adjusted EPS midpoint $12.35, operating cash flow ~$1.85B.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K via EDGAR, period ended 2026-01-02, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,750,000,000; capex $125,000,000; SBC $95,000,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $1,530,000,000 = $11.77/share** (dcf_numbers.json base_oe_latest_per_share $11.7692)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $1,257,000,000 — below the conservative figure because net working capital absorbed $356,000,000 in FY2026 (financials_history.csv delta_nwc); the two definitions bracket the same $1.3–1.5B zone, which raises confidence.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. OE/share history: FY2023 $6.54, FY2025 $8.83, FY2026 $11.77 — a real step-up, driven by mix: gross margin (fundamentals.json) went 13.98% (FY2023) → 16.36% (FY2025) → 17.72% (FY2026) as defense-tech products grew faster than labor services.
- Net debt $3,540,000,000 (dcf_numbers.json; basis LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations+DebtCurrent), plus lease liabilities $694,000,000. Shares are shrinking: diluted 136M (FY2025) → 130M (FY2026) → 127M (current-YTD weighted), share CAGR −1.97%/yr — buybacks are a genuine per-share tailwind and are already credited in the growth blend (+1.97pp on the revenue components only, per engine 5.4).

**Base used = latest fiscal year OE/share $11.7692, via base_override (see OVERRIDE).** The three candidate bases, all from this run's computed outputs:
- Engine normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): **$8.8309** — this is the FY2025 figure; the median window is anchored before the FY2026 margin step-up completed.
- Latest FY (FY2026, audited): **$11.7692** — chosen. Its cash quality is clean: OCF $1,750,000,000 sits almost exactly on net income $1,448,000,000 + D&A $290,000,000 = $1,738,000,000 (financials_history.csv), so the year is not flattered by a working-capital release.
- TTM through Q2 FY2026 (ttm.py): **$16.2441** — rejected, see STALE_FY under FLAGS.

## OVERRIDE — base (bounded authority (c))
- **Declaration:** judgment.json carries `base_override = {value: 11.76923076923077, kind: n/a (base_override), source: "This run's dcf_numbers.json base_oe_latest_per_share, built from financials_history.csv FY2026 row: OCF $1,750,000,000 − capex $125,000,000 − SBC $95,000,000 = conservative OE $1,530,000,000 over 130,000,000 diluted shares", reason: ...}` — built exclusively from figures this run's engine outputs printed, construction quoted here.
- **Why not the median:** the median ($8.8309) is the FY2025 print. Two consecutive audited years of mix-driven step-up sit after the window's anchor years: gross margin 16.36% → 17.72% (FY2025 → FY2026, fundamentals.json), operating income $1,827,000,000 → $2,109,000,000, ROIC proxy 16.94% → 19.10%. Q2 FY2026 corroborates the new level rather than a one-year spike: revenue +7.2% YoY, backlog +5.4% with funded backlog +44%, and guidance raised. The TPR/DGX precedent in this sweep: a median anchored on pre-step-change years is the distorted base when the latest audited FY is corroborated.
- **Why not TTM:** see STALE_FY — the TTM OCF surge is working-capital timing, with TTM net income actually down YoY.
- **Measured impact:** on the median base this same configuration prints weighted IRR 12.63% / IV@15% $99.56 (Tier C, preliminary run); on the chosen base, 15.72% / $132.68 (Tier B). On the rejected TTM base it would print 20.27% / $183.13 (Tier A). The override moves the tier, so the verdict below is sized to the conservative end and the method range (C→B on defensible bases) is the honest headline. score.json's override_impact block carries the machine-measured version.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow
Justification: incumbency, a cleared workforce and a $48.71B backlog are real advantages, but the customer is a monopsonist that recompetes the work, the core product is cleared labor that scaled rivals also supply, and the measured returns only stepped up two years ago.
- FOR: $48.71B backlog (~2.8x TTM revenue of $17,577,000,000, fundamentals.json) with funded backlog up 44% YoY to $10.22B — multi-year revenue visibility few services peers match; incumbency on mission-critical classified programs (Navy SMIT network, intelligence infrastructure) where past-performance ratings and an already-cleared workforce are formal bid discriminators and take years to replicate; scale and portfolio breadth ($17.6B revenue across defense, intelligence, health and civil) that lets it bid primes-sized integrations; mix shift into differentiated defense-tech products is lifting gross margin (13.98% FY2023 → 17.72% FY2026) and the ROIC proxy (fundamentals.json roic_proxy: 9.95% / 10.47% / 9.78% / 3.89% across FY2021–FY2023-era years, then 16.94% FY2025 and 19.10% FY2026).
- AGAINST: the US government is a monopsonist customer that recompetes contracts on price — Leidos has litigated Navy pricing on SMIT, and recompete losses are a standing feature of this sector (Booz Allen, CACI, SAIC, Parsons and the primes contest every award); through-cycle ROIC was ~10% and the FY2023 print was 3.89% — the 17–19% of the last two years is not yet proven through a budget cycle, so it does not support a 7+ score under the rubric; even after the mix shift, gross margin is 17.72% — a services margin, not a product franchise margin; federal budget and efficiency pressure (terminations, insourcing pushes) hits the whole revenue base at once; growth leans on M&A (Entrust) and buybacks rather than organic pricing power — Q2 organic revenue growth was +3.9% against +7.2% reported.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5.4 final run (2026-10-16)
Growth sanity check (written reasons): the engine's blended growth is 8.55% (rev CAGR 5y 7.00%, 3y 6.17%, latest rev YoY 3.20%, OE/share CAGR 2y 33.87% — the OE CAGR is one of four blend components and does not dominate; the blend is revenue-anchored with the +1.97pp buyback adjustment on revenue components). Recent prints: revenue TTM +3.52% YoY (fundamentals.json), Q2 FY2026 +7.2% reported / +3.9% organic, FY2027 revenue guidance midpoint $18.3B vs FY2026 $17,107,000,000. OE/share can outgrow revenue near-term on the ~2%/yr share shrink plus mix, so the base start of 8.55% is at the optimistic-but-defensible edge and is kept unadjusted; the bull start (13.55%) requires the FY2025–26 margin expansion to continue, which is why it carries 25% and not more; the super-bull start (20.55%) sits *below* FY2026's actual OE/share print (+33% YoY, $8.83 → $11.77) with a written reason: that print is a one-time margin step-up annualizing, not a repeatable growth rate, and revenue guidance (+7% at the midpoint) caps what OE can compound at. Default offsets (−12/−5/0/+5/+12pp), default OE multipliers (0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25) and default probabilities (10/25/30/25/10) were kept. Price $124.85.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −3.5% | 0.75 | Budget cuts / recompete losses bite; margins give back the mix gains | $56.44 | 7.90% |
| Bear | 25% | 3.5% | 0.90 | Revenue grows at the TTM print; OE/share grows only via buybacks | $90.73 | 11.61% |
| Base | 30% | 8.5% | 1.00 | Blend growth: mix + buybacks on mid-single-digit revenue growth | $124.01 | 14.92% |
| Bull | 25% | 13.5% | 1.10 | Defense-tech mix keeps expanding margins; Defense book-to-bill 2.2 converts | $167.50 | 18.77% |
| Super bull | 10% | 20.5% | 1.25 | Margin step-up repeats; backlog converts at raised-guide pace for years | $252.78 | 25.09% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $132.68 (+6.3% vs price), IV@12% $178.30, IV@20% $92.00, IV@25% $69.83, weighted IRR 15.72%, base-case IRR 14.92%**
- **Tier by numbers: B — barely.** Bear→bull band: C (11.61%) → B (18.77%). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 9.43%, terminal value 19.87% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.48x, net debt 2.31x the pinned base OE (3.08x the normalized median OE), 9.4 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.4 months ago): ttm.py was run and its legs are quoted in full — OCF: FY $1,750,000,000 − prior YTD $544,000,000 + current YTD $1,094,000,000 = **TTM $2,300,000,000**; capex: FY $125,000,000 − prior YTD $51,000,000 + current YTD $63,000,000 = **TTM $137,000,000**; SBC: FY $95,000,000 − prior YTD $46,000,000 + current YTD $51,000,000 = **TTM $100,000,000**; shares (current-YTD weighted diluted) **127,000,000**; **TTM OE total $2,063,000,000 → $16.2441/share**. The TTM pin was then **rejected as the base, with the reason stated**: the TTM window's OCF (+54.88% YoY, fundamentals.json TTM block) is working-capital timing, not earnings power — over the same TTM window net income *fell* 1.85% YoY to $1,376,000,000 and operating income printed $2,030,000,000, *below* FY2026's $2,109,000,000, while management's own FY2027 operating-cash-flow guidance (~$1.85B) sits well below the $2,300,000,000 TTM OCF. Capitalizing $16.24/share would book a receivables/payables swing as permanent earnings (it would print a Tier A — rejected). The latest audited FY is used instead (see OVERRIDE); its OCF ≈ NI + D&A check shows no such distortion.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023: net income differs from OCF by >40%): found and named — non-cash impairments. FY2023 net income attributable was $199,000,000 against OCF of $1,187,000,000 (financials_history.csv) because FY2023 operating income of $621,000,000 absorbed $596,000,000 of goodwill impairment charges and $91,000,000 of asset impairment charges (FY2023 results reconciliation: as-reported operating income $621M + $36M acquisition/integration/restructuring + $202M amortization of acquired intangibles + $91M asset impairments + $596M goodwill impairments = $1,546M non-GAAP). The impairments are non-cash and never touched OCF, so the OCF-based conservative OE series used throughout ($6.54/share in FY2023) is uncontaminated; the divergence flatters neither the base nor the growth blend's OE leg beyond what the filed OCF actually was.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.48x super-bear IV): real — the range between a recompete/budget bear case and a continued margin-expansion bull case genuinely is this wide for a contractor at a mix inflection. Confidence is capped at medium (make_score clamps it), and the verdict is sized to the bear end.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (preliminary run, on the median base: net debt 3.08x normalized OE): balance sheet stated from the filing outputs — net debt $3,540,000,000 (debt basis LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations+DebtCurrent) plus lease liabilities $694,000,000, against FY2026 conservative OE of $1,530,000,000: 2.31x the pinned base OE, 3.08x the median OE. Leverage is investment-grade-manageable but real: in the bear cases (OE mult 0.75–0.90) debt service is covered by a $48.71B backlog's cash conversion, yet there is no room for a large debt-funded deal on top of a recompete shock. The flag does not fire on the final pinned base; the exposure is recorded here regardless.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier C 11.61% vs bull tier B 18.77%): the verdict spans the 15% hurdle — the base case itself prints 14.92%, just under it, and only the probability weighting (which credits the bull tail) carries the headline to 15.72%. Any position must be sized to the bear end: bear IV@15% is $90.73, 27% below the $124.85 price.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the *range* across defensible bases: standardized median $8.83 → Tier C (12.63%, IV@15% $99.56); latest audited FY $11.77 → Tier B (15.72%, $132.68); TTM $16.24 → Tier A (20.27%, $183.13) on a base rejected here as working-capital timing. Anyone quoting the A without the TTM caveat is hiding the ball; anyone quoting the C is ignoring two audited years of mix shift.
- Quality is decent and improving, not elite: SBC is small ($95M FY2026, ~5% of OCF), capex is light ($125M), buybacks shrink the count ~2%/yr, and the dividend is covered many times over by OE. The earnings risk is not accounting — it is procurement: every dollar of revenue is re-bid, and the FY2023 goodwill impairments ($596M) are the scar tissue of paying for growth that procurement then repriced.
- Margin of safety is thin on the chosen base: weighted IV@15% $132.68 is only 6.3% above the $124.85 price, the base case alone does not clear 15% (14.92%), and on the standardized median base the stock clears 15% only below $99.56. A buyer at $124.85 is paid if the margin step-up merely *holds*, and is exposed if it reverses.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: B** (weighted IRR 15.72% on the latest-FY base; method range C→B across defensible bases — the range is itself the finding)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the FY2026 base's cash quality, medium-low on how much of the margin step-up persists; WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD caps confidence at medium regardless)
- One-liner: Quality government-services compounder at a mix inflection, moat 5/10 — clears 15% only on the latest audited FY base (weighted IRR 15.7%, IV@15% $132.68 vs $124.85) and only barely; on the standardized median base it is a C that clears 15% below ~$100, and the bear case ($90.73) sits well under the price — size it to the bear end.
